proxy_language: Old Prussian (West Baltic), with Lithuanian/Latvian and Proto-Baltic reconstruction as supporting evidence
proxy_rationale: The Amber Court is a fictional later court on the Baltic amber coast. The only attested language of the historical Baltic amber coast (Sambia/Samland) is Old Prussian, known from the Elbing Vocabulary (c. 1400), Simon Grunau's word lists, and the 16th-century Catechisms (Enchiridion 1561). Corpus is small and scribal spellings are German-influenced, so confidence is medium; gaps are filled from East Baltic (Lithuanian, Latvian) and Proto-Baltic reconstruction, marked with asterisks.
phonology: Vowels: a e i o u, long ā ē ī ō ū (written with macron or circumflex in the Catechisms), diphthongs ai au ei eu ia ua ui. Consonants: p b t d k g; s z (spelled s/ss/sz); sz /sh/ and z /zh/ in some scholarly notation; m n l r; w (/v/); j /j/; h only in loans. Palatalization contrasts are poorly attested. Stress was probably mobile and is not written.
phonotactics: Open or closed syllables (CV, CVC, V, VC). Word-final consonants common, especially -s (nominative), -n (accusative), -an/-in. Clusters such as st, sk, sp, tr, kr, pr, gr, dr, wr occur word-initially; sl, sm, sw, sn also occur. Geminates appear in German-influenced spellings (-ss-, -tt-) but are not phonemic. No word-initial ng or rr. Nominatives often end in -s, -is, -us, -as, -ai, -ei (m/f plural).
orthography: Use normalized scholarly Old Prussian: a e i o u, macron long vowels, w for /v/, j, sz and z for the sibilants, k not c, no q/x. Plain lowercase Latin is sufficient; macrons optional (the audit permits them).
morphology: Inflected IE language with nominative case endings. Masculine o-stems: -s/-as (deywas 'god'), feminine ā-stems: -a/-o (swintan, acc.), i-stems -is, u-stems -us. Genitive singular -as/-is/-s (e.g. deiwas, dēiwas 'of god'); accusative -an/-in/-un; plural nominative -ai, -ei. Verb: infinitive -t(wei), 3rd person -t. Adjectives agree in gender, number and case, ending like nouns. Diminutives -in-/-ik-/-ell- (rarely attested, borrowed from Baltic patterns). Agent nouns in -ikis/-nikis/-ins (compare Lith. -ininkas, -ėjas).
compounding: Compounds are head-final: modifier stem + linking -o- or bare stem + head noun (e.g. Elbing 'wosbalsnis'-type structures, Old Prussian ' gaylis ' 'white'). Genitive phrases are preferred over compounds: head noun + genitive or genitive + head noun. 'X of Y' = X + Y-genitive (e.g. deiwas 'of god'). 'Y-maker/keeper' = Y-stem + agent suffix (-ins, -ikis, -nikis). Place names built with -kaym 'village' (cf. Lith. kaimas), -pil 'castle' (Pilsāts, pilis), -wald-, -nov- 'new'.
noun_phrase_order: Adjective before noun (swints deiws 'holy god'); genitive modifier before or after its head noun, with prenominal genitive more common in the Catechisms; demonstrative before noun (stas deiws 'the god').

notes: Proxy is chosen because Old Prussian is the only attested language of the amber coast; names are modelled on its inflected structure, but roots not securely attested are borrowed from East Baltic (Lithuanian, Latvian) and flagged as reconstructed. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word unless the language is Goidelic.
